dedupe_keys.name: ntia its sigmf ntia namespace open metadata extensions for rf measurement data

description: This ITS news article announces open metadata extensions, an 'ntia' namespace for the Signal Metadata Format (SigMF), that let RF measurement datasets be shared and reused. It explains that the OPEN Government Data Act, signed on 14 January 2019, requires federal agencies to publish data in machine-readable formats with metadata, that ITS has published spectrum measurement collections for decades and that these are used to validate propagation models for spectrum sharing, frequency management and planning of telecommunications systems. ITS's older proprietary metadata formats were replaced by SigMF, a standard started at the DARPA Brussels SDR Hackfest in early 2017 and now supported by the GNU Radio Foundation, which is generic enough to describe any recording of a digitised time-series signal. Producer: ITS, the research laboratory of the US National Telecommunications and Information Administration; the article is dated 2 April 2020. Coverage: a metadata standard, applicable worldwide. Access: a public news article that links the extension documents. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence text read. Caveats: the page describes the extensions and does not itself contain measurement data. Simulation uses: consistent metadata make RF measurement data reusable for validating propagation and spectrum-sharing models. Related record: ITS legacy radio propagation data (data-its-legacy-radio-propagation-data).
